newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices drop on Tokyo, yen rebound.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices drop on Tokyo, yen rebound.

text.p: Thai rubber prices slipped as prices fell on the Tokyo market and the yen rebounded, traders said on Wednesday.
Benchmark RSS3 was quoted around 113.00 US cents a kg for July shipment and at 114.00 cents for August, compared with 115.00 and 117.50 respectively on Friday.
"The market is quiet as buyers were sidelined. They expected prices to come down further before placing orders," said a Hat Yai trader.
Others said some buyers were waiting to see where prices would go with the government expected to start buying at new intervention prices of 29.00 baht a kg this week.
One trader with a major rubber firm said he was sceptical whether the scheme would help to prop up the prices.

"What I think will happen is the government will be very selective on quality and the quality of unsmoked sheet grade 3 and grade 4 at the moment is not very good. Therefore, the purchase amount will be limited by this constraint," he said.
"At the end, a big amount of rubber will be in the market and shippers and exporters will have to buy at market prices which are much lower that that offered by the government," he said.
